question.text: Two parallel plate capacitors of capacity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>C</mi></math> are connected in parallel combination and charged to a potential difference <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>18</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The battery is then disconnected and the space between the plates of the capacitor of capacity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> is completely filled with a material of dielectric constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn></math>. The final potential difference across the combination of capacitors will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>.

solution.text:
The charge on the capacitor is given by q=CV.

Initial charge on C=18CV

And initial charge on 3C=54CV

Let final common potential difference =V'

When a dielectric of dielectric constant k is introduced between the plates of the capacitor the capacitance becomes k times.

Applying conservation of charge,

9CV'+3CV'=18CV+54CV

⇒12CV'=72CV⇒V'=6 V
